title: Which other numbers get both idli and vada?
description: The multiples of three and the multiples of five are written in two rows, and the numbers that sit in both rows are circled. They are fifteen apart, and Keeko's doubt, that fifteen is the only idli-vada number, is broken.
teaching_notes: One idea: a number that is a multiple of two numbers at once is a common multiple, and the common multiples of three and five keep coming. Watch for students who stop at the first one they find.

source: Which is the first number for which the players should say idli-vada
video_script.why: The child sees that the numbers which get both words sit in both lists of multiples, keep coming, and are called common multiples.
video_script.substitution: A number that sits in the list of multiples of two numbers is a common multiple of them.
video_script.anchor: the idli-vada game of the book: the first idli-vada number is fifteen
video_script.wrong_answer: fifteen is the only idli-vada number
video_script.wrong_move: Keeko says fifteen is the only idli-vada number, because the game finds it first. The two rows carry on, so thirty, forty five and sixty also sit in both and the doubt is struck.
video_script.payoff_line: Fifteen, thirty, forty five, sixty and more are the common multiples of three and five

final_answer.spoken: fifteen, thirty, forty five, sixty and more, called common multiples of three and five

never_show: the name common multiples before the answer
maths_rules: the common numbers are 15 apart: 30 - 15 = 15, 45 - 30 = 15, 60 - 45 = 15, so they are the multiples of 15
video_script.design: One idea: numbers that sit in both lists of multiples are the common multiples. Assumes the child knows multiples. Wrong idea: fifteen is the only one. The two rows stay on the board to the end.

beats.on_screen: a small title card From your book; the circle of children and the words idli, vada and idli-vada; the number 15 is marked as the first idli-vada

marks.book: the small title card From your book appears
marks.first: the number 15 is marked as the first idli-vada
marks.ask: the words which other numbers, and what are they called appear

narration: <bookmark mark='book'/>This is a question from your book about the idli-vada game.
<bookmark mark='first'/>The first number that gets idli-vada is fifteen, a multiple of three and of five.
<bookmark mark='ask'/>Which other numbers get idli-vada, and what are such numbers called?

beats.on_screen: the question stays on the board

marks.think: Keeko sits at the corner of the board

narration: <bookmark mark='think'/>Think and tell.

beats.on_screen: two empty rows, one above the other, ready to hold the multiples of 3 and the multiples of 5

marks.rows: the two empty rows appear, one for threes and one for fives
marks.both: a gap is drawn between the rows to show a number can sit in both

narration: <bookmark mark='rows'/>Write the multiples of three in one row, and the multiples of five in another row.
<bookmark mark='both'/>A number may sit in both rows.

beats.on_screen: Given: idli-vada is said for a multiple of 3 that is also a multiple of 5; the first one is 15

marks.given: the rule and the first number are written under the word Given

narration: <bookmark mark='given'/>Given, idli-vada is said for a multiple of three that is also a multiple of five. The first one is fifteen.

beats.on_screen: To find: the other idli-vada numbers, and their name

marks.find: the words To find are written

narration: <bookmark mark='find'/>We have to find the other idli-vada numbers and the name for them.

beats.on_screen: Step 1: multiples of 3 up to 60 in the top row: 3, 6, 9, 12, 15, 18, ..., 57, 60

marks.threes: the top row fills with the multiples of 3 up to 60

narration: <bookmark mark='threes'/>Step one, write the multiples of three up to sixty: three, six, nine, twelve, fifteen and on.

beats.on_screen: Step 2: multiples of 5 up to 60 in the bottom row: 5, 10, 15, 20, 25, ..., 55, 60

marks.fives: the bottom row fills with the multiples of 5 up to 60

narration: <bookmark mark='fives'/>Step two, write the multiples of five up to sixty: five, ten, fifteen, twenty and on.

beats.on_screen: Step 3: the numbers that sit in both rows are circled: 15, 30, 45 and 60

marks.both: a number in both rows is circled and joined by a line to its twin

narration: <bookmark mark='both'/>Step three, look for the numbers that sit in both rows, because those get both words.
<bookmark mark='four'/>Fifteen, thirty, forty five and sixty are in both.

beats.on_screen: Step 4: the gaps between the circled numbers: 30 - 15 = 15, 45 - 30 = 15, 60 - 45 = 15; they carry on: 75, 90, ...

marks.gap: each gap between neighbouring circles is marked as 15

narration: <bookmark mark='gap'/>Step four, take away to find each gap. Thirty take away fifteen is fifteen, and forty five take away thirty is fifteen.
<bookmark mark='more'/>The numbers are fifteen apart, so they carry on with seventy five, ninety and more.

beats.on_screen: Answer: 15, 30, 45, 60, ... are the common multiples of 3 and 5

marks.name: the words common multiples are written under the box

narration: <bookmark mark='ans'/>Fifteen, thirty, forty five, sixty and more are the common multiples of three and five.
<bookmark mark='name'/>A number that is a multiple of two numbers at once is called a common multiple.

beats.on_screen: Keeko with a raised hand beside the boxed answer
narration: <bookmark mark='hand'/>Keeko has raised a hand. Let us check the doubt and solve it.

beats.on_screen: Keeko's doubt in a bubble, then struck through; both rows stretch on past 15 and 30, 45, 60 are circled

marks.fix: both rows stretch on and the circles at 30, 45 and 60 glow
marks.more: the circles at 30, 45 and 60 are lit one by one

narration: <bookmark mark='doubt'/>Keeko thinks fifteen is the only idli-vada number.
<bookmark mark='fix'/>But the game does not end at fifteen, because the children keep counting on.
<bookmark mark='more'/>Thirty is a multiple of three and of five too, and so are forty five and sixty.
